newsitem.title: USA: Technology seen key in Bankers Trust deal.
newsitem.headline: Technology seen key in Bankers Trust deal.

text.p: Bankers Trust New York Corp's plan to buy the institutional trust business of NationsBank Corp was viewed positively on Wall Street, although some analysts said the move reinforces the need to spend heavily on technology.

"This confirms their recent pronouncements that their processing division is not for sale and that they would more likely embellish it," said George Salem, analyst at Gerard Klauer Mattison, referring to Bankers Trust.

The analyst said one of the attractions is that it is a growing business. For Bankers Trust in particular, he said, the business "provides stability to an income statement which is pretty volatile now."

In its first-quarter earnings release April 17, Bankers Trust said client processing services contributed $13 million of net income in the first quarter of 1997, down $5 million from the first quarter of 1996.
Overall net income was $169 million versus $138 million a year ago. Revenues in the client processing business rose $14 milllion to $196 million.
Bankers Trust said that the decline in net income reflected higher operations costs and growth in staff expense.
In a research report on Bankers Trust April 22, Salomon Brothers analyst Diane Glossman wrote that "..the custody business is quite large, but requires major systems investment."

Asked what kind of technology commitment Bankers Trust is making, a Bankers Trust spokesman, Alan Hanson, said the company spends $500 million a year on technology with about one-third going to global trust and custody and cash management.
In a research report after the earnings, Brown Brothers Harriman analyst Raphael Soifer said Bankers Trust expects to complete work on a "very expensive" global custody system by the end of 1997.

Analysts said that companies like Bankers Trust, State Street Corp and Bank of New York Co Inc that have committed thsmelves to the business and the spending that goes with it will benefit from economies of scale as other players withdraw.

The transaction with NationsBank announced Friday involves the transfer to Bankers Trust of approximately 465 master trust and custody accounts with corporations, not-for-profit institutions, public funds, and Taft-Hartley funds. The transaction. a definitive agreement, is subject to regulatory approval and is expected to be completed in the second quarter.
Terms were not disclosed although Bankers Trust said it will not have a material affect on earnings.

An industry source said that typically in such transactions a final price is not detemrmined until some time after the deal closes, and the price is based on how much of the accounts are retained by the buyer.

Bankers Trust said it has been providing institutional trust services since its founding in 1903 and is now the fourth largest custody provider worldwide, with a subcustodial network that covers more than 60 countries.
